title: One aggregated entry refusal: which underlying, for what reason, how many times
description: Source: src/box/entryAlerts.ts EntryAlertLedger. AGGREGATED BY (underlying, reason) ON PURPOSE: 354 identical refusals of one name for one reason are ONE fact with a count of 354, not 354 notifications. This is the only surface that carries BOTH the symbol and the reason — `metrics.execution.rejection_categories` is a process-lifetime metric label space and therefore structurally cannot carry a symbol (that is the cardinality explosion src/box/executionFaults.ts exists to prevent); `box_execution_attempts` rows carry the symbol but are written ONLY when filled_leg_count > 0 or an emergency unwind occurred, so a refusal that never reached the market persists nothing; and the ENTRY_REJECTED_* trade events are throttled per candidate, so a name refused hundreds of times leaves a handful of rows. Keying by underlying is bounded here (see entry-alerts.schema.json `dropped_groups`) in a way it can never be in a counter map.

underlying.description: The underlying that was refused, as the board reports it (e.g. NIFTY, RELIANCE). Never blank — an attempt with no resolvable underlying is recorded as the literal string "(unknown)" rather than as an empty group nobody can act on.

reason.description: The refusal reason from the CLOSED parent-attempt taxonomy (BoxParentAttemptReason: every BoxExecutionFailureReason, plus the ten ExecutionFaultClass technical classes, plus persistence_unavailable and the legacy internal_error). Deliberately NOT constrained to an enum here: the taxonomy is closed in TypeScript and asserted exhaustively by the entryAlerts unit suite, and pinning the list in two places is how the two come to disagree — which is exactly the drift that caused real reasons to be reported as unknown_internal_error.

category.description: WHAT KIND of problem this is, which decides whether a human must act. `market` is ordinary churn (the price moved, the edge closed) and is deliberately NOT actionable — a bell that rings for it trains an operator to ignore the bell. `operator_action` means a setting or an operator decision is refusing entry and nothing will trade until it changes (a spent session budget, a blocklisted name, a met inventory ceiling). `infrastructure` means a dependency is unhealthy (feed, database). `fault` means our own code or an unclassifiable failure.

actionable.description: True for every category except `market`. Precomputed by the backend so clients cannot each invent their own definition of urgent and then disagree about what the badge means.

count.description: How many times this exact (underlying, reason) pair was refused since the ledger was last reset. Never throttled or sampled: the hook that feeds this is called on every refusal precisely so the count is a count and not an estimate.

first_at.description: Epoch milliseconds of the FIRST occurrence. Published alongside last_at so a long-standing condition is distinguishable from one that just started — the same count means very different things across ten seconds and across four hours.

last_at.description: Epoch milliseconds of the most recent occurrence.

last_detail.description: The refusing layer's own detail for the MOST RECENT occurrence, whitespace-collapsed and truncated to 240 characters. The newest is kept rather than the first, because a stale sentence beside a fresh timestamp is worse than none. null means the layer supplied no detail, never that there was nothing to say.

last_candidate_key.description: The most recent candidate key (underlying|expiry|K1|K2|DIRECTION), so a specific strike pair can be found and checked. null when unknown.

remedy.description: What the operator should DO about it — always a real sentence, including an explicit "no action" where that is the honest answer. Derived from the reason by an exhaustive map in src/box/entryAlerts.ts, so a new reason cannot be added without someone deciding what a human is supposed to do when it fires.
